main_text.p: Nicolaitis, vti Tertullianus. Ante Valentinia-nos collocat Isidorus, sed Augustinus Epipha-nium secutus est,qui Heracleonitis subiicit.Irenaeus libro i. cap. 34. demum post Gnosticos & Valentinianos exortos esse scribit, a quibus tan quam è coenoso fonte impurissimus riuus fluxerunt. Ergo circa annum a Domino passo 132. a nobis constituentur longe post Nicolaitarum hærefin,a qua tamen,vt scribit Epiphanius,dogmatis & erroris occasionem acceperunt. Maxime in AEgypto,vt aliæ multæ,viguit,ex cuius regionis & gentis idololatria & moribus initiu videtur sumpsisse. AEgyptij enim Ibes,Croco-dilos,& huiusmodi ferarum genera pro diis habuerunt, atque etiam tunc colebant,vt docent M.Tull.Cicero,Plutarchus,Iuuenalis Satyr.14. & alij:quorum exemplum hi secuti Draconem serpentémque venerati sunt alio quidem,quàm AEgyptij,prætextu,sed tamen serpentem,id est, immanem & homini funestissimam beluam. Sæpe vero Satan magnas præstigias fecit hominibus non tantum fidelibus, sed etiam infidelibus per serpentem, quod in Adamo primo parente nostro manifestissimum est. & de ea re scribit author prophanus in Pseudoalexandro. Durauit autem vsque ad tempora Iustiniani primi Constantinopolitani imperatoris hęc hęrefis,& postea quoque,quàquam est fœdissima.De iis enim meminit l.xj.C.de Episcop.audientia.& l.Arrii ni.C.de Hæretic.

page.notes: The "z" in the left margin and the "*" in the right margin are printed marks without text; they are transcribed as bare notes. The ")" after "colubrum" is printed as it stands. The long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. The large initial "S" of "Sæpe" is joined to the word. The first line of the page continues from page 46. The final word of the page breaks as "sce-" and continues on the next page. Some letters in the scan are slightly blurred (notably "hęc hęrefis" and the ligatures in "fœdeque"); they are read as printed but may be unreliable.
